checks.description: Counts deterministic cache subleaves, legacy descriptor bytes and AMD legacy L2 presence. Reports missing cache information conservatively; leaf 2 may include TLB descriptors.

fix.how: Present a coherent CPU policy: match vendor, brand, feature dependencies, cache and topology to the configured vCPUs and real model. Do not advertise instructions the guest cannot execute.
fix.chimera: Validate Xen CPUID policy together with cpuidmon -s. Host-derived SMBIOS does not change CPUID. Test both guests and every advertised CPU leaf after masking.

checks.description: Guarded SIDT/SGDT/SLDT/STR/SMSW. The historical rules (al-khaser idt_trick/gdt_trick: base high byte 0xFF; str_trick: TR = 0x4000) are applied to native 32-bit processes only. UMIP makes the instructions fault or return emulated values; on 64-bit systems discrimination is very low.

fix.how: Corroborate descriptor observations against the exact OS and CPU. Preserve architectural privilege/UMIP behavior rather than spoofing arbitrary addresses; modern descriptor placement has little standalone value.
fix.chimera: Xen and guest UMIP policy may fault or emulate these instructions. cpuidmon -s cannot alter descriptor placement. Do not modify guest tables to satisfy a historical heuristic.

checks.description: Records BSF/BSR zero-source destination values and ZF, plus 16-bit SHLD count 17. Only incorrect defined ZF behavior is detected; undefined output values are never treated as universal emulator signatures.

fix.how: Correct violations of defined instruction semantics in the emulator. Keep undefined flag/destination observations separate from portable detection decisions and validate against multiple physical CPUs.
fix.chimera: Xen normally executes these integer instructions on hardware. Android-x86 under TCG needs independent validation; cpuidmon masking does not fix instruction semantics.

fix.how: Mask exposed hypervisor interfaces consistently, including relocated ranges and interface signatures. Remove dependent guest enlightenments only after checking boot, clock and interrupt behavior.

checks.description: VMCALL and VMMCALL at CPL3 with an invalid call number (0x0BADC0DE), guarded. Bare metal raises #UD for both; Xen and KVM return -EPERM to user mode without a fault. Records whether RAX changed.

fix.how: Make CPL3 VMCALL/VMMCALL raise #UD in the guest as on bare metal; this needs a hypervisor change.
fix.chimera: Xen 4.19 hvm_hypercall() answers CPL>0 hypercalls with -EPERM instead of injecting #UD; hiding it needs a Xen patch. cpuidmon does not affect it.

checks.description: Guarded VirtualPC version query 0F 3F 07 0B with EAX=1 and EBX=0; records whether it returns or faults.

checks.description: IN from port 0x5658 with EAX='VMXh' and commands 0x0A (get version) and 0x14 (memory size), guarded. Outside VMware the IN faults (#GP at CPL3); a 'VMXh' echo in EBX is VMware.

fix.how: Restrict user-mode VMware backdoor access where supported, after checking guest-tools dependencies. An expected privilege fault is a negative response, not a probe failure.
fix.chimera: Xen should reject these VMware-specific I/O requests. Investigate unexpected successful signatures in nested or compatibility configurations; cpuidmon and firmware strings do not govern this port.

checks.description: Interleaved LFENCE/RDTSC latencies for leaves 0,1,7,0x40000000,0x40000100,0x80000000; compares largest and smallest medians. Research heuristic also triggered by real CPU leaf-cost differences; not VMAware CPUID_SIGNATURE.

fix.how: Calibrate on comparable bare metal and minimize exits and host scheduling noise. TSC offsetting/scaling and exit-cost compensation require coordinated hypervisor work; a static offset cannot remove per-exit cost and clock compensation must remain consistent across vCPUs and clocks.
fix.chimera: Not fixable by configuration. cpuidmon -s rewrites CPUID values but turns every CPUID into a vm_event round trip to dom0 (about 35x the plain exit cost, see the G2 numbers); masking through the Xen CPUID policy instead (xl.cfg cpuid=, verify that Xen 4.19 honours clearing the bit for HVM) removes the monitor cost but not the ~2.5k-cycle exit. Hiding the exit itself needs Xen-side TSC compensation for CPUID exits, which Xen 4.19 does not have; tsc_mode, TSC scaling and vCPU pinning do not remove per-exit cost. CHIMERA G2 measurements (2026-10-29, i7-13700HX host): median RDTSC;CPUID;RDTSC 2398-3720 cycles on the Xen HVM guest without an introspection monitor and 92530-94514 cycles with DRAKVUF cpuidmon -s, which forwards every CPUID to the dom0 monitor; al-khaser's avg10 rule fired 1000/1000 in every configuration, dom0 included (1590-1964 cycles).

params.name: timing.leaf_iterations
params.meaning: Samples per leaf; clamped to 100..20000 and four seconds.

params.name: timing.leaf_ratio
params.meaning: Largest/smallest median ratio; local research default, clamped to 1..1000; calibrate on matched bare metal.

checks.description: Pinned to one CPU, 2000 warm-up rounds, then raw RDTSC;RDTSC (floor) and RDTSC;CPUID;RDTSC pairs plus independent al-khaser ten-round integer averages. Replaces the separate CHIMERA cpuid-timing harness.

params.name: timing.iterations
params.meaning: Requested paired samples; clamped to 100..1000000 and a four-second sampling budget.

params.name: timing.trials
params.meaning: Independent ten-round average trials; clamped to 1..1000 with a separate four-second budget.

params.name: timing.vmexit_cycles
params.meaning: Cycle threshold for the median and avg10 trials; clamped to 1..1e9. Default is al-khaser rdtsc_diff_vmexit; zero or backward counters are anomalous.

params.name: timing.introspection_cycles
params.meaning: Median above which CPUID is classified as trapped to an introspection monitor; clamped to 1..1e10. Default from the CHIMERA G2 measurements (2.4-3.7k plain Xen HVM, 92-95k with DRAKVUF cpuidmon -s).

checks.description: Measures each native wait against TSC, monotonic/QPC, wall and tick/boot clocks. Detects early completion or disagreement beyond tolerance plus 20-ms quantization slack. Clocks can share hardware; coherent acceleration remains undetectable.

fix.how: Disable sleep acceleration for fidelity runs, or coordinate all wait APIs and time sources while preserving monotonicity, timeout semantics and thread scheduling. Compare accelerated and normal runs.
fix.chimera: CHIMERA optional time acceleration can shorten Sleep/NtDelayExecution/waits or Linux nanosleep/select while leaving TSC or shared time unchanged. Disable it for baseline tests; coherent acceleration can still evade these comparisons.

params.name: timing.sleep_ms
params.meaning: Requested milliseconds per API; clamped to 50..500. Windows uses Sleep, event WaitForSingleObject and NtDelayExecution; Linux uses nanosleep and select.

params.name: timing.sleep_tolerance
params.meaning: Fractional clock/early-wait tolerance, local policy clamped to 0.01..0.8; also adds 20 ms for Windows tick quantization.

params.name: timing.sleep_tolerance

checks.description: Research side channel. Batched (8 calls per clock read) latency of a failing call that registry/file monitors trace (Windows: NtOpenKey on a random absent key; Linux: openat of a random absent name in /), of a cheap syscall (NtQueryInformationProcess / getpid) and of a user-mode arithmetic reference. Detected when a median exceeds the traced floor or the traced call is far slower than the cheap one. Moderate confidence; cannot name a monitor.

fix.how: Trace fewer calls, or only the calls an analysis needs; each traced call costs a trap. Keep in-guest filter drivers and audit rules to what the image needs.
fix.chimera: Every DRAKVUF breakpoint trap (syscalls, regmon, filetracer, procmon plugins) is a VM exit plus a vm_event round trip to dom0, which costs tens of microseconds per call. Disable plugins that are not needed for a run, and prefer the syscalls plugin's filter (-S) to tracing every system call. The cost cannot be hidden from the guest.

params.name: instrumentation.iterations
params.meaning: Batches per series; clamped to 100..20000 and a three-second budget.

params.name: instrumentation.min_latency_ns
params.meaning: Per-call median (ns) above which a call is treated as trapped; local research default (untraced failing opens cost about 0.3-5 us), calibrate per host.

params.name: instrumentation.latency_ratio
params.meaning: Traced-call / cheap-syscall median ratio for selective tracing; local research default.

checks.description: Declared clock resolution and 10000 observed monotonic clock increments, including API overhead and backward counts. Coarse clocks alone do not identify a sandbox.

fix.chimera: cpuidmon -s changes CPUID values, not VM-exit latency; its handling can add cost. Xen TSC mode or vCPU pinning alone cannot erase that cost. Validate any Xen/DRAKVUF compensation against raw RDTSC, RDTSCP and OS clocks; retain residual-risk reporting.

params.name: timing.resolution_ns
params.meaning: Warn if minimum observed positive increment exceeds this local 1-ms threshold; clamped to 1..1e9 ns.

checks.description: TSC frequency against the monotonic clock in repeated bounded 20-ms busy windows; reports MHz statistics and relative range. Busy calibration avoids using a possibly accelerated sleep.

params.name: timing.tsc_windows
params.meaning: Busy calibration windows; clamped to 3..20, each capped at two million clock polls.

params.name: timing.tsc_drift_fraction
params.meaning: Relative (max-min)/median frequency tolerance; local research default, clamped to 0.001..1.

checks.reason: Unsafe: the EIP_OVERFLOW probe can crash Xen guests. Never executed, even under deep profile.

fix.how: Do not run this destabilizing probe. Use safe guarded instruction and timing observations and review the hypervisor separately.
fix.chimera: Excluded because Xen guest stability is a binding requirement. A process-level signal/exception guard cannot recover a guest/kernel crash.
